geeklist.title: 2023 Dice Tower East Virtual Flea Market
geeklist.description:
[size=18][b]It's time to plan and organize for The Exchange[/b][/size]
[center][imageid=7585546 large][/center]
[b]When is the VFM Exchange?[/b] Thursday, July 6th 9:00AM-10:00AM EDT in the Antigua rooms. Buyers and sellers must attend the Exchange unless both parties have agreed to other arrangements. See the [thread=3070454][b]VFM Admin Thread[/b][/thread] for more details on managing alternative arrangements. ⚠️[b]Opening Crowd Control:[/b] For everyone's safety, no exchange activity will be permitted in the Antigua hallway prior to the exchange opening. This will be enforced. ⚠️[b]Important:[/b] Pallet jacks, heavy transport devices, and anything with metal/steel wheels may not be used on hotel grounds; these devices can damage the outside tile and interior flooring. Light duty pull wagons with rubber or plastic wheels are OK.
[b]Can I still buy and sell?[/b] Yes, but all BIN offers are considered Late Offers. See the [thread=3070454][b]VFM Admin Thread[/b][/thread] for the definition of a Late Offer.
[b]I am done selling, should I withdraw my unsold items?[/b] No. We would prefer you just leave unsold items in place and politely decline any late offers. Please handle late offers on a case by case basis.
[b]What else?[/b] • [Buyers] While not required, I highly recommend [b]placing exact change for each seller in an envelope[/b], on the outside of the envelope include the seller's real name, BGG name, cell number (if you have it), and an itemized list of the games you are expecting, include notes on any special meetup arrangement if not the scheduled exchange. This simple preparation will make your purchases go much more smoothly. • [Sellers] Double check the condition of sold games including all promised components. Post-it notes are your friend, [b]make a sign with your BGG name and real name[/b], be sure to have a checklist. Sellers meeting outside the scheduled exchange should reconfirm arrangements with buyers.
[b]Other Exchange Tips:[/b] • Wearing a distinctive hat or some article of clothing might sound silly, but it can be a big help in standing out in the crowd • Bring a sign with your BGG ID and Real Name. • Bring a hardcopy checklist of your sales and purchases • Optional: don't be afraid to stand on a chair and shout out people's names, you won't be the only one. (DTE Admin is not responsible for people following silly advice like standing on chairs) • If you are buying and selling many games, try to bring a partner. One partner can be the seller, that person stays stationary under a sign with the pile of outgoing games, the other partner is the buyer that roams the room completing purchases. It is much easier for buyers to locate stationary sellers. • If you are buying and/or selling many games consider bringing a wagon
[b]What happens if I can't find my Buyer or Seller?[/b] It's very rare, but there are some cases of last minute no-shows. I highly recommend exchanging cell phone numbers, at a minimum every buyer and seller has a BGG account and can be reached by GeekMail. If all else fails I can verify if a person has picked up a badge, but this should only be done as a last resort.
[b]Important Links[/b] [thread=3070454][b]VFM Admin Thread[/b][/thread] [geeklist=314772][b]VFM Wish List[/b][/geeklist] [url=https://www.yulgame.com/Vfm/Items/314755][b]VFM Alphabetical List 1[/b][/url] [user=Carnage994]Eric Bettan[/user] version. [url=http://bgg.activityclub.org/tools/vfm.html?listid=314755]][b]VFM Alphabetical List 2[/b][/url] [user=JeffyJeff]Jeff Michaud[/user] version. [url=https://www.yulgame.com/Vfm/AddItems/314755][b]VFM Posting Tool[/b][/url] [user=Carnage994]Eric Bettan[/user] version.
[b]Currency:[/b] All transactions are assumed to be in [u]cash[/u] ($US). If you are accepting/offering payment via cash app, crypto, or other means, please make that very clear in your listing or offer before finalizing a sale.
[b]Please [u]do not delete[/u] items from this list[/b]. See the [thread=3070454][b]VFM Admin Thread[/b][/thread] for instructions on how to properly withdraw an item.
⚠️ Use of this GeekList as a seller, buyer, or in any other capacity constitutes an agreement to abide by all instructions on this page as well as all instructions and terms of service located [thread=3070454][b]here.[/b][/thread].

[b]⚠️Sellers:[/b] The commission note in the VFM header and on the Admin page has been updated. BGG [u]will not[/u] automatically send you an invoice. Your current ad fees can be found [geekurl=/market/account/payfees][b]here[/b][/geekurl], however, [b]DO NOT[/b] pay the fees until after the exchange. In the very rare case that a sale does not go through as planned, such sales can be canceled to correct the commission due (see header). Please note that while a commission has always been required by BGG the Mark Sold and Ad Fee functionality to automate this process are new this year and evolving. As usual, if you have questions or concerns, please post them on the [thread=3070454][b]Admin Thread[/b][/thread].

Whenever I see someone trying to flip one of the Dice Tower freebies, I envision somebody who waits in line at a soup kitchen to get a free meal, and then shows up the next day in front of the same soup kitchen and tries to sell it at a profit.
There’s something distasteful about trying to make a profit on others’ generosity.
I saw one person who was nice enough to offer it for free to the first person to ask for it, and all I could think of was, I hope that person doesn’t turn around and try to resell it on the flea market.

What is the proper way to mark something if traded? I marked my first item as "withdrawn" with comments that it was traded, but that also removes it from all the alpha tool searching stuff. The other party marked his as "SOLD" -- I thought for $0 but it must have been for a minor amount. I just did another trade and marked it as the minimum ($1) price -- great, because it still shows up on trackers, but it wonks out the bgg marketplace average sale price.
Is there a "standard" I should be adhering to? I don't see this on the VFM admin thread.

[q="kaelius"]What is the proper way to mark something if traded? I marked my first item as "withdrawn" with comments that it was traded, but that also removes it from all the alpha tool searching stuff. The other party marked his as "SOLD" -- I thought for $0 but it must have been for a minor amount. I just did another trade and marked it as the minimum ($1) price -- great, because it still shows up on trackers, but it wonks out the bgg marketplace average sale price.
Is there a "standard" I should be adhering to? I don't see this on the VFM admin thread.[/q] Interesting.... been doing this for years and a trade has never come up, now it's happened twice.
There is no standard. I wouldn't recommend using the sold button, as you pointed out, it will skew the BBG price tracking and you'll be charged a minimal commission. Withdrawn works, but as you pointed out, the alpha tools won't see it as a transaction. I can suggest one temporary work around, put "Traded (not sold)" in your item description and delete any reference to price. The alpha tools still look for the legacy keyword "sold" so they will treat it as a sold item and as long as there is nothing in the description that looks like a price they will leave that field blank. I will talk to the tool developers and ask them to consider adding "Traded" as a keyword and handling it in some appropriate manner.

On a similar topic to deleted item, I placed a low-ball offer days ago on a game. (I normally don't do that.) The seller never responded, so I assumed it was rejected, which is fine. Rushed for time this morning, I just deleted my offer; no other replies were on the item. Is that okay? (I didn't think about this until after the fact.) Or should I have edited my reply to something like just 'withdrawn'?

While I'm on a roll, when a seller reduces an item, I like when they cross out the old price and add the new price. I know most sellers do that, but there have been others who have not been doing that. (I'm not mentioning names because I like them. 😁) Is there a policy on marking reduced prices? Or is the strikeout text just a courtesy?

[q="CPBelt"]While I'm on a roll, when a seller reduces an item, I like when they cross out the old price and add the new price. I know most sellers do that, but there have been others who have not been doing that. (I'm not mentioning names because I like them. 😁) Is there a policy on marking reduced prices? Or is the strikeout text just a courtesy?[/q] As an unofficial answer. I do strike through when I reduce an item to either make people feel like it’s a deal or to show that I’m trying to price reasonably as the flea market goes on.

[q="CPBelt"]While I'm on a roll, when a seller reduces an item, I like when they cross out the old price and add the new price. I know most sellers do that, but there have been others who have not been doing that. (I'm not mentioning names because I like them. 😁) Is there a policy on marking reduced prices? Or is the strikeout text just a courtesy?[/q] Showing price reductions is just a convention, it is not a requirement. I try to interfere as little as possible in individual listings. If it's fair to buyer and seller and if it doesn't break the list operation, it's probably OK. That said, it's a missed marketing opportunity... people love a deal, at least I love deals, I think showing the mark-down helps move games.
We’ve reached over 100 pages of games already! Crazy

[q="Forsak3ngaurdian"]We’ve reached over 100 pages of games already! Crazy[/q]
Last year with the 1st DTE VFM, we started the list on May 9 and hit 100 pages on June 12, with far more promos listed IIRC. I'm looking at the list now, so it may be off due to people deleting entries.
2022 VFM ended with 266 participants (buyers & sellers combined), 5417 items, with 2477 sold (45.7 %). We had many promos last year compared to this year. States courtesy of Eric's awesome script.
This year so far, 173 participants, with 2492 items, 717 sold (28.8 %) . Far more 'auctions' this year, with less activity on them from what I can see on Eric's script. Not sure what that is saying about users this year.
IIRC DTE has the same # of people as last year? Lots of variables at play. Someone can do the percentage sold per day. I'm not up to all the math right now. I gotta go buy some games. 😉

Yeah, I don't really see the point of having auctions run all the way up to the week of the event. In my experience, auctions get little to no action until the final 24-48 hours. I've done a few items as auctions this year simply because I'm not confident in how to price them. I wanted to give people enough time to see the items, and research if necessary, so picked a mid June end date. But even that is starting to feel way too long to me :laugh:

I always try to research when posting so my BIN on the auctions are already good deals (I'll adjust and lower as needed). I lean this way because then people who see the deal and don't like to haggle have an option to not be outbid. I guess in a way having a lower starting bid and a BIN is haggling with myself LOL.

[q="jmsmith2434"]Yeah, I don't really see the point of having auctions run all the way up to the week of the event. In my experience, auctions get little to no action until the final 24-48 hours. I've done a few items as auctions this year simply because I'm not confident in how to price them. I wanted to give people enough time to see the items, and research if necessary, so picked a mid June end date. But even that is starting to feel way too long to me :laugh:[/q] Honestly, I don't bother participating in the auctions. I don't want to wait a month and a half to know if I've won something. And if another deal comes along in the meantime, but I'm waiting weeks to find out if I'll be the winner on the first one... It's just not worth bothering with for me.

I imagine items for bid are just skewing the sale numbers to start. I'm bidding on 12 items as it is and one other one ended already. Its a really long time to wait, but I can see why sellers might want to do that. I'd prefer not to do auctions, but potentially getting a game for $5 or $10 has its appeal.

Well it looks like with only a month to go -- I will be lowering all my games to get them to sell... it reminds me of the last 19 minutes of the flea market.. 🙂

Hey Folks, Just a reminder, to prevent flooding various channels please don't self-promote here or on other DT managed social media outlets (FaceBook, Discord, etc...) Starting this Saturday (June 3rd) I will promote the VFM as a whole on a weekly basis with a particular emphasis that sellers are cutting prices and making deals. Now would be a good time to review the entire list. etc...
Is there a preferred way for lowering your item prices? I know there will be a flood of changes from here on out.

[q="JohnnyC1971"]Is there a preferred way for lowering your item prices? I know there will be a flood of changes from here on out.[/q] Nope, do whatever you think might work. I like to show serial markdowns eg: BIN [-]$30[/-], [-]$25[/-], $20 I think it helps buyers to see the price history but that is just a matter of style. You can lower starting bids, switch from auction to fixed price (assuming no auction activity), offer bundle discounts, etc...

[b]A Message for VFM Sellers, and nosey buyers[/b] 😉
Once a week, starting from this Saturday, I am going to advertise the VFM in the FaceBook group and other channels suggesting that buyers should review the entire list as sellers begin to mark down prices and make deals during the final countdown to the convention. If you are inclined to review your pricing, now would be a good time.
Also, as a reminder, to prevent a flood of messages as we get close to the end, please refrain from self-promoting specific items on FB or here in the chat.

I am working on some assumptions regarding non-BIN buyer offers, but I want to verify if they are correct.
If as a buyer I make an offer that is below the BIN, I am assuming that that offer can be retracted at any point up until the seller accepts it, is that correct? Otherwise, it would be like a floating IOU that could be redeemed at any point the seller wanted. A practical ramification of this would be if after making the offer that was not acknowledged by the seller, another seller offered the same game and I wanted to purchase it from them instead. In such a circumstance I would not feel obligated to be held to the original offer I made if the seller hadn’t accepted it.
The second situation would be if I made an offer as a buyer and the seller refused the offer. The assumption I’m working on in that situation is that they cannot at some point turn around and say they changed their mind without first verifying whether I still wanted to go through with the transaction. Is this correct?

[q="Gankatron5000"]I am working on some assumptions regarding non-BIN buyer offers, but I want to verify if they are correct.[/q]
This sounds reasonable. In all cases, just try to be reasonable. If I am selling a game and decline a bid, then I consider that bid over. But if later I decide it is actually ok, I as a seller would just DM the bidder and ask if they are still interested.

Agree that confirmation should go both ways
In the situation if you make an offer, don't hear back and want to withdraw, you should comment and say "offer withdrawn" or something along those lines (rather than deleting a comment)

[q="Gankatron5000"]If as a buyer I make an offer that is below the BIN, I am assuming that that offer can be retracted at any point up until the seller accepts it, is that correct?[/q] Yes, this case is already addressed in the ToS. An offer below the BIN or SB (a "low ball" offer) is not binding on either party until both sides accept and yes, the low ball offer may be retracted at any time.
[q="Gankatron5000"]The second situation would be if I made an offer as a buyer and the seller refused the offer. The assumption I’m working on in that situation is that they cannot at some point turn around and say they changed their mind without first verifying whether I still wanted to go through with the transaction. Is this correct?[/q] Assuming you are still talking about a low ball offer, then yes, both sides must reconfirm. Loosely speaking, any arrangement between buyer and seller is acceptable (low ball offers, bundles, trades, sweeteners, hybrid deals, etc..) but any arrangement outside of the original item description requires a virtual handshake between both parties and either can withdraw at anytime prior to that handshake.
Only a BIN or bid above SB are automatic and do not require conformation from the seller. There are reasons for this, it protects both the buyer and seller. Once a BIN is made the buyer can't hop to a cheaper item and say "well, the original seller never confirmed so I was free to withdraw" and at the same time the seller can't slow walk confirmations hoping for a higher bid on what was posted as a fixed price.
There is an exception to automatic acceptance of BINs... when we reach the late or "travel" phase of the VFM where sellers may already be packed and may be on their way to the con. Any offers made within two weeks of the con are considered late offers and require double confirmation (ie: a handshake) The start of the late phase will be announced with major changes to the header.

I had a No Show for a few of my items that were sold. How do I remove them as sold so that I won't pay the BGG Fee for these items?

According to the VFM admin list:
• Click the "Sold for $XX" button • Click the "Sale ID" number • Click the "Mark Canceled" button

[q="Korrun"]According to the VFM admin list:
• Click the "Sold for $XX" button • Click the "Sale ID" number • Click the "Mark Canceled" button[/q]
I sadly don't see a Mark Canceled button. I'm worried it is because the items sold back in May and BGG has already assessed fees and sent invoices for these sales. I'm only out a few $, but it stings after already having brought the items to the con and having to bring them back home.

Did you already pay the invoice? If not, on the invoice list you can click on the item and there is a cancel button when it opens up that item invoice. I had to do this when BGG glitched and invoiced me multiple times for the same item. If you’ve already paid the invoice then I’m not sure if there is an easy way to get refunded.

It worked for me and immediately adjusted my invoice. Make sure you are clicking on the "Sold for $XX" button first" on the item that you are trying to cancel, then click on the "sale ID" number. I just did it a few days ago.
It appears after a certain length of time the cancel sale button is no longer available. I see the option on some of my items that sold later.

Really hemmed and hawed about putting this up. Great Kramer/Kiesling collection and area control game with a unique time track for collecting bonuses and abilities.[/I] [B]FP:[/B] [-]$65[/-] $55
item.comment: What is your definition of “very good”? Any dicernable wear and tear?

The way they did the heat transfer of their tiles is that little dings show from fingernails and such pretty much any time you use it. You have to be looking for it to notice, but I didn't want to classify it as Like New. The original box was damaged in transit, so Game Brewer sent me a replacement. You won't be able to tell a difference there. The storage solution trays and such that come with the game are pretty wobbly, but that's just kind of how they are. If you bid for this and get it and are dissatisfied by its condition, let me know and I'll take it back.

I already see the comraderie and such at Dice Tower ... take a look at my current sale list (https://www.yulgame.com/Vfm/Items/314755?Seller=kaelius&Status=NotSold&Sort=Name) ... if there's something left there that's $40 or less that's of interest, tell me and it's yours -- I'll simply give it to you to try and make it right. item.comment: Would you be interested in trading for Sentinels of the Multiverse or Hidden Leaders?

Jake, No thank you to Sentinels or Hidden Leaders. However, I noticed you asked a similar question on Tsuro. I looked over your collection and although you didn't have any marked as "for trade", you didn't seem to be a big fan of Scythe. Would you want to trade Scythe for both Empires of the Void II and Tsuro?

I'm sorry I didn't even take notice that you were the seller of both games. Yeah I would love to make that trade. However, I should inform you that my copy is an unplayed ding and dent copy from Barnes and Noble. [imageid=7532861] [imageid=7532867] I guess I should mark a few for trade. Marvel United, Tides of Madness, Smartass, Cover your Kingdom, Tranquility (dinged also), Last Aurora, Thief's Market, The Crew, Hidden Leaders, Sentinels of the Multiverse, and a review copy of Intergalactic Ace are what I know I am looking to exchange as of right now. Plan on going through some of my other played games as well. Space Cadets: Dice Duel, Exodus: Proxima Centauri, Mare Nostrum: Empires, Lost Cities: The Board Game, and Near and far are some of yours I am looking at. Let me know!
Done. I will trade you Empires of the Void II and Tsuro for your copy of ding and dent copy of Scythe.

item.comment: Interested in promo A and Leeghwater if you'd break it up.
Not interested in breaking it up. Thanks though.
As a follow-up, does this copy have any of the production issues of the wheel, water droplets, or misaligned 3d board?

I got the "fixed" wheels and I think the corrected droplets but honestly I was so put off by the whole experience that I haven't been motivated to play it again (I'd played it at PAXU and enjoyed it). My 3D board does have misalignment issues, not enough to make it unplayable or anything but enough to make me feel bad for buying it.
Thanks for the reply. If you change your mind about splitting it, let me know.
Still interested in Leeghwater if you'd split.
Thanks but no. Its all integrated together and the expansion box has long been discarded. If the expansion is tough to find though you can always keep the parts your missing and flip the rest.
Honestly, I think it would be pretty hard to move one of the misaligned boards. Not something I'm willing to take on. I can wait for the expansion to be restocked. Thanks for the reply though.

Okay Jim I’ll buy for $40. Thanks.

item.body:
[B]Version:[/B] [B]Language:[/B] [B]Condition:[/B] Very Good - [I]spent a few hours trying to count this out. I picked it from someone else, and afaik, this is a KS release -- has the Kickstarter extras of [thing=223914][/thing] and [thing=228552][/thing] expansions, the KS Accessory Pack, and some promo cards. If I counted right (a bit hard with everything mixed together), I *think* it is missing 5 crystals, but there are so many extras from the KS extras pack, this is completely irrelevant to game play and I'm not 100% convinced it is [missing them]. The wiki pages for The Outer Dark and The Void have 2 different counts for the # of nemesis cards that should be present -- both match one of the #s (and clearly not hte other 🙂). No manual for the expansions or the extras -- I strongly suspect that there never was one. Fantastic shape, I suspect it was never played, some small bits are still sealed.[/I] [B]SB:[/B] $45 [B]BIN:[/B] $60

item.comment:
Hi Atticus, Could you please edit this item to show that it is sold to me? I had asked Bob Gallo about it, and here is our conversation:
Hi Bob, I successfully BIN’ed (is that a word? LOL!) three items, but my buyer’s name (“bmacp”) is showing up as “n/a” in two of them on the list. How can that be fixed? The two items are Really Loud Librarians (#2754) and Word Slam (#2521). —————————- Hi Bonnie, the seller (not you) should edit their item description and add one of the following:
Sold to: bmacp Avatar Bonnie MacPherson @bmacp or Sold to: bmacp
Which will properly show your name on the alpha tools and will look like this on BGG: Sold to: bmacp Avatar Bonnie MacPherson @bmacp or Sold to: bmacp
Strictly speaking we don't require that sellers tag their buyers, not everyone is comfortable with BGG formatting codes but it really is as simple as copy/pasting the code above and it is very, very helpful for both buyers and sellers when trying to review their transactions.

item.comment: I’ll BIN for $10. This looks like stupid fun. 😄

Hi Jeremy, Could you please edit this item to show that it is sold to me? I had asked Bob Gallo about it, and here is our conversation:
Hi Bob, I successfully BIN’ed (is that a word? LOL!) three items, but my buyer’s name (“bmacp”) is showing up as “n/a” in two of them on the list. How can that be fixed? The two items are Really Loud Librarians (#2754) and Word Slam (#2521). —————————- Hi Bonnie, the seller (not you) should edit their item description and add one of the following:
Sold to: [user=bmacp][/user] or Sold to: [user=bmacp]bmacp[/user]
Which will properly show your name on the alpha tools and will look like this on BGG: Sold to: bmacp Avatar Bonnie MacPherson @bmacp or Sold to: bmacp
Strictly speaking we don't require that sellers tag their buyers, not everyone is comfortable with BGG formatting codes but it really is as simple as copy/pasting the code above and it is very, very helpful for both buyers and sellers when trying to review their transactions.

item.comment: Hi Steph, would you have any interest in talking trade of this + Fairy Land (#3803) + Milestones (#3880) for a 3d-printed insert for a game of your choice? I won't have time (and cost wise it wouldn't work out) for something huge like Frosthaven, but if you know of something you might be interested in (or maybe a few small ones), I'm happy to chat. I'm not a business or anything, just a dude with a couple of printers that usually work, but have done this a couple of times locally and on reddit and folks seem pleased. A few nice things you generally get from replacement inserts -- organization, possibly boxs+lids for bits so you can store vertically, and/or ability to store sleeved cards.

[B]Condition:[/B] Very Good - [I]Opened from shrink, played only 1x on same night. Cards have some flex, but that's how they came.[/I] [B]BIN:[/B] $10
FWIW, I often do a write-up for myself and a few others on why I keep/get rid of games ... here was my note: [i]Dragon's Gold. 1@3p, 42min. This plays up to 6 people and I think would really play best both (a) with 5-6 people and (b) folks that enjoy talking, negotiating, possibly arguing, tricking, manipulating, etc. I don't have either (a) or (b) around normally. At 3 people, it was sort of "meh". Trader's Tomb, a very similar game, is posted on one of the "hidden gems" pages I follow, so I think there's definitely possibility here, and I might reacquire it in the future. I think it has a lot of potential with the right group.
Short view: multiple people end up selecting the same pile of goodies, that starts a 1min timer, if they can't allocate them in a way everybody agrees on then no one gets any at all. Repeat until all goodies have come out, been assigned to piles, and then taken by players or discarded because the folks on that pile couldn't agree. [/i]

Sorry, nothing on the list stood out to me. If you change your mind on Valley of the Kings though let me know.

[q="Cwyszynski"]Sorry, nothing on the list stood out to me. If you change your mind on Valley of the Kings though let me know.[/q]
Darn, but totally understand. Seems to be a lot of discounting going on. If you'd take $20, also up for that.

[q="Cwyszynski"]Meet in the middle at $25?[/q] Super tempting, but I've spent enough already that I probably ought not to. Another option, if it was of interest, though ... any chance you have interest in trading for a 3d-printed board game insert? I'm doing a trade with someone else for one of these, but I *ought* to be able to finish it up and complete another before I leave for FL. I've made that offer to a couple of folk, and can't do all of them if more than 1 more pan out, but thought I'd mention it just in case. (If that's interesting, there's a few places to look and see what's possible, one is going directly to thingiverse.com and/or printables.com and just typing in the game name; another is to start on the curated bgg list here: https://boardgamegeek.com/geeklist/186909/3d-prints-board-games)
Buy it! It's a great game!!! You won't regret it!😝

If that had come up about four months ago I'd have been interested, but that's when I got my own 3D printer. If you change your mind let me know. I'm more or less local so I can put it in my bag as late as the evening of July 4.
Hey Chris. I'll take it for $25. (although, I keep adding this to my own sale list, if something else is more interesting in trade or partial trade, still open for that discussion).
Sold for $25, I’ll keep checking your list though, just in case.

item.body:
Condition – Like New – Removed from shrink but never punched or played
SB: $15 Auction ends – July 1st
item.comment: $25 since he doesn't state when on the 1st it ends
Rick, pease clarify if “Auction ends - July 1st” actually means when July 1st occurs or otherwise. 😆

[q="Gankatron5000"]Rick, pease clarify if “Auction ends - July 1st” actually means when July 1st occurs or otherwise. 😆[/q] Nice try attempting to snipe this, but this isn't ebay. I'm pretty sure there isn't a time stated because that is absurd. Zhi was the high bidder for 2 weeks, so it's perfectly in his rights to bid back over you. We don't even know Rick's time zone.
Allen, did you withdraw your $30 bid?
Also, please try to remain civil. Asking for clarification when the auction ends is perfectly acceptable behavior, this isn’t Facebook so keep your outrage to yourself please.

pretty sure Allen is not the who is having the issue of "keep your outrage to yourself". I don't think there is any other bid on any of the 5000+ items on this VFM, that tries to timestamp itself with a last second bid, a few secs before the auction to try to snipe the bid. I am currently in germany on a work trip, so technically your bid came in 5 hours and 5 secs too late since it was way pass midnight here. But I like to be a sporting person, so if you Gankatron5000, can provide me a link to any other auction in this FVM when someone was allow to snipe a bid, secs (i will even allow up to 5 mins) before the end time (which even isn't exactly stated in this auction) and was ACCEPTED as the winner, then I will happily withdraw my bid of $25 dollars. If not then this auction is on like donkey kong!

Good morning all – please accept my humble apology for not making my end-of-auction time clear. Without boring you all with the details, I am juggling some personal issues at the moment, so keeping up with my auctions has fallen lower on my priorities list. Again, I’m sorry for that.
With that said, I had always intended to let my auctions run through the end of the day today, July 1. So the auction will end at MIDNIGHT tonight, July 1, US Eastern time.
Again, apologies to all. And by all means, let’s try to be one big, happy family. 😊

The problem with your guys’ attitudes is that you didn’t bother waiting to see if I would have had an issue with Rick saying the auction was not intended to be over at midnight.
Since there was no indication of exactly when or how the auction would end other than “July 1st”, I made sure to specifically indicate when my bid was made in case it was intended to be over at midnight and then asked Rick for clarification with a laughing emoji to indicate a lightened mood.
The whole Facebook outrage post vibe is referring to Allen’s first in righteous indignation about sniping instead of waiting to see if there was even conflict on my end.
I can tell you that if Rick indicated it was an ongoing auction instead of being over at midnight of July 1st I would’ve responded in my typical fashion during this VFM with the single word “Understood”, so I also don’t appreciate the righteous attitude.
This particular game tends to sell for over $50 US, but I’ve actually seen it over 100 in the past, so Rick has every right to try to get the most money he can for it during an auction.
It should be pointed out that Allen is trying to school me on the etiquette of this auction in the face of having made a $30 bid after yours and then deleting it, something that is clearly in violation of the flea market rules.
This is referred to as irony.
EDIT: Note that I was writing this post prior to Rick’s clarification, so this was not a response to Rick’s post. 😉

[q="NocturnalAllen"]I'm pretty sure there isn't a time stated because that is absurd[/q]
You say that but…
There you go, thank you Rick for the clarification, and my response is, understood.
To you other guys, if you notice Rick has indeed specified a fixed time that ends at midnight and doesn’t continue in an open ended fashion, meaning that if somebody places a high bid at 11:59 and 55 seconds tonight they likely would win the auction.
It also would have meant that had he intended for the auction to end at midnight yesterday then leaving a last-minute bid would have been appropriate in sharp contrast to your anti-sniping protestations.
Feel free to bid among yourselves, I’ll leave it to you guys, and Allen, feel free to re-bid the original $30 that you then deleted, again ironically during an auction that you were arguing was still live, but please recognize that none of this outrage would have been present had you just been patient enough to wait for Rick’s clarification of when his auction actually ended, but where’s there fun in that, right?

[q="Gankatron5000"]The problem with your guys’ attitudes is that you didn’t bother waiting to see if I would have had an issue with Rick saying the auction was not intended to be over at midnight.
Since there was no indication of exactly when or how the auction would end other than “July 1st”, I made sure to specifically indicate when my bid was made in case it was intended to be over at midnight and then asked Rick for clarification with a laughing emoji to indicate a lightened mood.
The whole Facebook outrage post vibe is referring to Allen’s first in righteous indignation about sniping instead of waiting to see if there was even conflict on my end.
I can tell you that if Rick indicated it was an ongoing auction instead of being over at midnight of July 1st I would’ve responded in my typical fashion during this VFM with the single word “Understood”, so I also don’t appreciate your attitude.
This particular game tends to sell for over $50 US, but I’ve actually seen it over 100 in the past, so Rick has every right to try to get the most money he can for during an auction.
It should be pointed out that Allen is trying to school me on the etiquette of this auction in the face of having made a $30 bid after yours and then deleting it, something that is clearly in violation of the flea market rules.
This is referred to as irony.
[/q]
Sorry English is not my first language, but from my small understanding of the word irony, would it not be a good example of irony for a person to state that the seller should try to “get the most for his money” while also being the same person trying to snipe the bid and pay less by placing a at the last minute to disallow counter bidding?

I’ve been traveling around Asia for the last 2 1/2 months so I also tend to apologize that I don’t speak the native language instead of expecting everyone to speak perfect English in their country, so I understand, but please don’t be sorry about that as I likely don’t speak your language. 🙂
I believe your misunderstanding isn’t so much around the word irony, but around the significance of the word sniping in the context of an auction with a fixed ending time and how that affects the seller’s profit.
It might be irony in this case if I implied the seller was entitled to the greatest profit margin while simultaneously arguing that their open ended auction should instead be closed at a specific time, as opposed to a more free-floating ongoing counter bidding process.
As Rick indicated he does intend for this auction to be over at a specific time, that is midnight today.
What you protest as sniping is actually allowing Rick to get the most possible money up to the last possible moment since the auction would not continue past his specified time.
I do understand though, that if you were the next to last bidder and somebody did make a bid at the last moment prior to the auction ending at midnight, that probably would be disappointing even though Rick would be making more money than your offer.
So, if somebody else happens to be the highest bidder moments before midnight EST tonight, and you wish to actually win the auction, I would suggest that you place a higher bid at the last moment and even bump it up a dollar or two just in case, which is what I did if you happened to notice.
I hope this makes sense to you.

Can y'all quit with the paragraphs of text? This is an auction.
$26.
I've spent way to much time reading this to not jump in with a bid. $31!
I bid 3 cannolis at 11:59 pm and 55 seconds.

Sold - to @Bentadams1 - for $31
(Sorry Gankatron, I'd love those cannolis, but I'm trying to lose a coup[le of pounds)
Well, you still probably deserve a consolatory cannoli for putting up with all the peripheral drama.
[q="Gankatron5000"]Well, you still probably deserve a consolatory cannoli for putting up with all the peripheral drama.[/q] And I can vouch that Rick is "one of us" and not part of Big Cannoli. 😎

[b]Beautiful one-of-a-kind Collectors Solid Pewter Fantasy Chess Set with board. [/b]Condition: Excellent [b]$250[/b]
This is a one of a kind collection of pewter pieces handmade from Perth Pewter in the USA. The board is solid wood with a glass top and pewter Dragon feet. These pictures don't do it justice. It's gorgeous! [imageid=6912578] [imageid=6912577] [imageid=6912576] [imageid=6912592] [imageid=6912593] [imageid=6912579] The board is 19.25" each side, with the playing area being 17". The dragon feet on the board extend it out to 21". And the board sits 4.5" high. Some of the tallest pieces are 6.75" tall. Some of the smallest are about 3" tall. A lot of the other pieces are around 4.5" tall.
Cash or Venmo/ PayPal. Can meet early or at VFM meet-up.
item.comment: Wow..that is a beautiful chess set! 😍

[q="BlueDane"]Dimensions?[/q] Thanks for asking ! The board is 19.25" each side, with the playing area being 17". The dragon feet on the board extend it out to 21". And the board sits 4.5" high. Some of the tallest pieces are 6.75" tall and some of the smallest are about 3" tall. A lot of the other pieces are around 4.5" tall. Hope this helps. It really is an amazing piece of work! 😊

This is for a 3d-printed Cthulhu themed dice tower, printables.com [url=https://www.printables.com/model/4946-cthulhu-dice-tower]model #4946[/url]. Afaik, since this is explicitly licensed for commercial use (see the site), it is fine to sell {if anybody knows different, please let me know}.
Dimensions: About 4.5" tall and 5.5" from front of tentacles to back.
Condition: like new Price: $12
Background: I've had fun printing a variety of dice towers for my wife and I try to out. We decide we don't like most of them for some reason or another, and so I give them away to friends or trade them out for games. This is one of those extras -- we find that we gravitate towards slightly larger models with bigger openings on top, but this seems to work just fine.
Images are of the actual item image gallery with multiple pics: https://postimg.cc/gallery/TnxsDYs [url=https://postimg.cc/WhxZL7sZ][img]https://i.postimg.cc/htt1mCw2/PXL-20230629-024840544-MP.jpg[/img][/url]
Sale ends July 2 (but I'll have it at the physical flea market on Sat too)

Afaik, since this is explicitly licensed for commercial use (see the site), it is fine to sell {if anybody knows different, please let me know}.
Dimensions: Big. About 7.5" tall and 3.5" square
Condition: like new Price: $25
Background: I've had fun printing a variety of dice towers for my wife and I try to out. We decide we don't like most of them for some reason or another, and so I give them away to friends or trade them out for games. This is one of those extras -- we find that we gravitate towards larger models (like this) but ones with really big openings on top so we can slam lots of dice in. The hole isn't huge on this one, but die make multiple rotations on the way down with an incredibly satisfying sound of travel.

Version: Brown box version that says "CATAN Boards" Language: Condition: Very Good
FP: $35
Comes with 5-6 player expansion middle piece.
Notes: This was part of two Kickstarters many years ago that have since been removed from the Kickstarter site due to conflicts between the KS creator and the license controller for catan. Initially it was officially licensed and later not. The money from the second Kickstarter was used to complete the first and the second mostly failed with the manufacturers distributing some of the rewards at an additional cost. I backed both campaigns but only got this reward for the first one.
This is compatible with at least the 4th edition and possibly other later editions (I only have the 4th). I believe the tile slots are larger than the 3rd edition. It also needs the punch out port pieces to populate the port slots.
I have kept the brown box which looks similar to this for storage of the boards:
[imageid=3018475]
It was the shipping box though so it still has a label and looks like it has been through the mail but I have kept it for storage of the boards.
Will be at official meetup and willing to meet outside of that as well as long as you make arrangements with me. I accept Paypal Friends and Family, Venmo F+F and cash.

Listing 1 final item. Home made 3D printed portable push your luck game. You know what it's called, call it what you like. I call this one I Just Can't Stop Stoppin! I made this for myself, it has enough components for 4 players. Plus extra pieces in case any get lost. All pieces fit inside the box, and the box can be used a dice tray during game play. I figure on the off chance someone wants it I will make myself a new one after the convention. No rules are included, you know where to find them. Or make up your own rules =) $25 (Expensive for what it is, but where else are you gonna get one? Over 50 pieces that each require labor of removing supports. Time and material cost I really can't give it away for less) [imageid=7599241 large]
item.comment: You did an awesome job with this! How much?
Price? I would love to have this, but am low on funds.
Price in the comments. $25 (Sorry but there is a bit of labor in here)
I potentially have time to make 1 more of these before the convention if I start today! I need to know asap though.
any pic of 4 player pieces all stacked on the same spot?
This one doesn't have all 4 in 1 spot, but they do stack. As can be seen here [imageid=7599279 medium]
[q="spidie2000"]This one doesn't have all 4 in 1 spot, but they do stack.[/q] I'm more concerned with how well it stacks with all 4 which obviously happens at least early game 🙂
BIN $25 if the pieces stack reasonably without falling over
We've been making print and play versions of this for a while now. Would be nice to play a "real" version.

They stack fine with all 4, I will take a picture. they do get a little bit of a lean with all 4 in 1 spot but won't fall over on their own. If someone tips them over with their hands that is another story.

btw you should upload your data files to one of those sites and add a 4th entry for [thing=41][/thing] to the geeklist
[listitem=5310580][/listitem]

[imageid=7599301] [imageid=7599302] Here is 4 stacked strait. And another pic with all 4 stacked with full lean to 1 direction. They wont fall on their own but they will with a little help. Just to be clear this is not a travel edition. I wouldnt play it in the car or airplane, they would for sure fall over.

[q="Korrun"]BIN $25 if the pieces stack reasonably without falling over[/q]
See above for the 2 pictures I uploaded of stacked pieces and let me know if you want it.

item.body:
[b]Withdrawn[/b]
[-][b]BIN Price:[/b] $10
[b]Condition:[/b] Good Condition
[b]Payment:[/b] Cash or Venmo[/-]

[size=18][b]This is it! The deal everyone has been waiting for at the very end of the VFM.[/b][/size]
[user=Pleady][/user] is the proud new owner of this tightly curated collection.
Not :d6-1:, not :d6-2:, not even :d6-3: promos, but more promos than you can count* for the single low, low price of [b]$5[/b]! Just read the FAQ's below:
[imageid=7601421 medium]
[b]I only want a few of these, can I buy them separately?[/b] No, you must take them all.
[b]OK, what if I give you $5, can I take only the ones I want?[/b] No, see the first point.
[b]There's a lot a glare in that picture, can you take a better one?[/b] No.
[b]OK, so, are there any good promos on that table?[/b] Probably not.
[b]So why don't you just give these away?[/b] Because commerce.
Hurry, a deal like this can't possibly last. While you're zooming in on the picture trying to count the promos you need, someone else is just gonna hit the BIN button.
⏱️In the incredibly unlikely event that someone doesn't jump on this once-in-a-lifetime offer, this deal expires at midnight, July 4th and will never be repeated or until the DTR VFM (whichever comes first).
*Any implied claim of countless promos should be considered hyperbole, you can probably count the promos, I just don't want to.
item.comment: Sold, thank you sir. Never has there been a better purchase in the history of VFM's.
